slides.title: Decision Tree: Introduction

visualInspection.notes: Supervised trees support classification and regression; hierarchical sequential tests partition data until pure or another stop. slides.title: Decision Tree: Anatomy

visualInspection.notes: Univariate tests use one feature; multivariate linear tests sum w_j*x_j+b and can create oblique hyperplanes. A univariate tree can use different features at different nodes. Most-informative refers to the chosen local impurity or MSE criterion, not proof of a globally optimal full tree. Classification impurity differs from regression squared-error objective. slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Decision Tree: Anatomy

visualInspection.notes: Visible partition uses horizontal y=2.5, then lower-region x=4.5. Lower-left leaf has four blue points and is pure; upper region has four red and two blue points, so is mixed despite red majority fill; lower-right has one red. Axis-parallel numeric paths define hyperrectangles, possibly unbounded; linear oblique tests give polyhedral intersections. Maximum depth, minimum sample count or insufficient impurity decrease can stop before purity. Pure training leaves can overfit. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Decision Tree: Strengths, and Weaknesses

visualInspection.notes: Tree strengths: visible simple rules and no usual need for feature standardization in ideal axis-aligned comparisons. Complete scaling invariance needs qualification for finite precision and transforms that change ordering. Ordinary constant-leaf regression can evaluate out-of-range inputs but does not extend a trend; prediction remains a leaf target summary rather than necessarily the last chronological target. High variance under small training changes can persist despite pruning; not a universal failure claim. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Random Forests: Introduction

visualInspection.notes: Forest ensembles combine randomized trees to reduce variance/overfitting under suitable diversity; averaging identical perfectly correlated predictions does not create the benefit. Randomization encourages diversity, not a mathematical guarantee every tree is unique or every dataset accuracy improves. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Random Forest: Building

visualInspection.notes: Bootstrap draws n rows with replacement from n original rows, retaining n draws but possibly fewer distinct observations. Examples [2,5,3,2,5] omit1,4; [3,1,1,4,3] omit2,5. Approximate omitted fraction is an expectation near e^-1 for large n, not an exact one-third in each sample. Derived finite-n nonselection probability (1-1/n)^n is explicitly a mathematical extension of the stated sampling process. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Random Forest: Parameters, Strengths, and Weaknesses

visualInspection.notes: Increasing n_estimators generally adds cost and may stabilize averaging, but does not guarantee monotonically better test accuracy. Setting max_features to every feature removes feature subsampling, not bootstrap randomness. The printed regression default log2(n_features) conflicts with the official RandomForestRegressor current default 1.0, meaning all features. The classifier sqrt default is distinct. Nearly always better is not demonstrated by a benchmark here. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Random Forest: Parameters, Strengths, and Weaknesses

visualInspection.notes: Axis-aligned forests usually do not need feature standardization, which does not eliminate other preprocessing needs. Trees can be built independently and n_jobs controls parallel jobs, not the number of trees. Memory/time comparisons and high-dimensional limitations depend on the problem. A regression forest can output predictions outside the observed input range; averaging leaf means does not extend a learned numerical trend beyond the training target range, and need not return the last chronological sample. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.

slides.lectureTitle: Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests
slides.title: Summary

visualInspection.notes: Summary lists tree tests, pruning, bootstrap and feature randomization, plus applications to terrain, fault diagnosis, UAV navigation and defect inspection. The universal statement that forests outperform a single tree on all robotics benchmarks is unsupported by evidence on this slide. Prototype-versus-production advice is a heuristic, not a mandatory or safety-validated deployment rule. Actual 1800-pixel rendering and footer inspected.
